title: Unit 06: Book-II Heroes Part 3 (Mustafa Kemal - Modernization of Turkey)
subject: english-12

questions.question: In Wilfrid F. Castle's biographical essay 'Mustafa Kemal', what was the geopolitical plight of Turkey at the conclusion of World War I in 1918?

options.A: The Ottoman Empire had conquered all of Europe.
options.B: The Ottoman Empire was utterly shattered, Constantinople was occupied by Allied fleets, and the Treaty of Sèvres threatened to partition the Turkish heartland.
options.D: Anatolia was transformed into an economic paradise.

questions.explanation: Following the Armistice of Mudros, Allied forces occupied Istanbul, Greek armies landed at Smyrna, and the Sultan was a powerless puppet.

questions.question: What official post was Mustafa Kemal appointed to by the Sultan's government in May 1919?

options.A: Ambassador to the United States
options.B: Inspector-General of the 9th (later 3rd) Army in Anatolia, tasked with disbanding Turkish rebel divisions
options.C: Minister of Foreign Affairs in Istanbul
options.D: Grand Admiral of the Ottoman Navy

questions.explanation: The Sultan sent Kemal to Anatolia to disarm patriotic guerrilla bands, but Kemal instead organized a nationwide resistance movement.

questions.question: What historic date marks Mustafa Kemal's landing at Samsun, universally celebrated as the beginning of the Turkish War of Independence?

options.B: 23 April 1923
options.D: 1 January 1918

questions.explanation: Kemal landed at the Black Sea port of Samsun on 19 May 1919, issuing the Amasya Circular to mobilize Turkish national sovereignty.

questions.question: Where did Mustafa Kemal convene the Grand National Assembly in April 1920 to establish a sovereign revolutionary government?

options.A: Istanbul (Constantinople)
options.B: Ankara (Angora) in the central Anatolian plateau
options.D: Trabzon

questions.explanation: Kemal established the new patriotic capital at Ankara, far from the vulnerable reach of Allied naval guns in Istanbul.

questions.question: What aggressive foreign invasion backed by the Allied powers did Mustafa Kemal crush to reclaim Turkish territory?

options.A: The Greek invasion of western Anatolia (Battle of the Sakarya & Great Offensive)
options.B: The Russian conquest of the Caucasus
options.C: An Italian amphibious landing in Cyprus
options.D: A Persian cavalry campaign

questions.explanation: Greek forces advanced toward Ankara, but Kemal defeated them at the 22-day Battle of Sakarya (1921) and drove them out of Izmir in September 1922.

questions.question: What treaty superseded the humiliating Treaty of Sèvres, establishing Turkey's modern sovereign borders in 1923?

options.A: The Treaty of Versailles
options.B: The Treaty of Lausanne
options.D: The Treaty of Paris

questions.explanation: The Treaty of Lausanne (July 1923) recognized total Turkish independence, abolishing the humiliating capitulations and foreign zones.

questions.question: What fundamental revolutionary step did Mustafa Kemal take regarding the ancient Ottoman ruling institutions?

options.A: He crowned himself Sultan of the Middle East.
options.B: He abolished the Ottoman Sultanate in 1922, proclaimed the Turkish Republic in 1923, and abolished the Caliphate in 1924.
options.D: He merged the government with the League of Nations.

questions.explanation: Kemal dismantled the six-century-old Ottoman dynastic rule, replacing it with a secular, democratic national republic.

questions.question: What cultural reform did Mustafa Kemal introduce regarding traditional Turkish attire?

options.A: He mandated that everyone wear military uniforms.
options.B: He abolished the traditional red felt fez and encouraged modern European hats and suits, while discouraging the veil for women.
options.C: He made turbans compulsory for civil servants.
options.D: He outlawed shoes and boots.

questions.explanation: The Hat Law of 1925 banned the fez, symbolizing Turkey's integration into modern world civilization.

questions.question: What radical linguistic reform did Mustafa Kemal implement in 1928?

options.A: He replaced the complex Arabic-Persian script with a modified modern Latin alphabet, traveling across Anatolia with a blackboard to teach villagers himself.
options.B: He banned the speaking of Turkish and adopted French.
options.D: He made English the sole medium of instruction in primary schools.

questions.explanation: Kemal introduced the Latin phonetic alphabet, vastly accelerating nationwide literacy; he personally toured towns with a portable blackboard to teach the new letters.

questions.question: What legal transformation did Mustafa Kemal enact regarding women's rights and family law in Turkey?

options.A: He adopted the Swiss Civil Code, abolishing polygamy, granting women equal rights in divorce, property ownership, and voting in parliamentary elections (1934).
options.B: He banned women from university education.
options.C: He prohibited women from entering courtrooms.
options.D: He eliminated inheritance rights for daughters.

questions.explanation: Kemal emancipated Turkish women, granting them full civil equality and political voting rights years before many Western European nations.

questions.question: What title was officially bestowed upon Mustafa Kemal by the Grand National Assembly in 1934 under the Surname Law?

options.A: Atatürk ('Father of the Turks')
options.B: Sultan-ul-Muazzam
options.D: Caesar of Anatolia

questions.explanation: The Turkish parliament unanimously awarded him the honorary surname 'Atatürk', meaning 'Father of the Turks'.

questions.question: In Castle's essay, how did Mustafa Kemal handle economic development in the new republic?

options.A: By selling all natural resources to British cartels
options.B: Through state-directed industrialization (Five-Year Plans), building railways, iron mills, textile factories, and a modern banking network without foreign debt
options.D: By shutting down agriculture to focus exclusively on tourism

questions.explanation: Under the principle of Étatisme (Statism), Turkey built sovereign heavy industries, ports, and national railways financed by domestic capital.

questions.question: What was Mustafa Kemal's famous national slogan advocating peaceful international diplomacy?

options.A: 'Conquer at all costs!'
options.B: 'Peace at home, peace in the world.' (Yurtta sulh, cihanda sulh)
options.D: 'Only military alliances ensure survival.'

questions.explanation: Kemal anchored Turkish foreign policy on peaceful coexistence, mutual respect of sovereignty, and regional non-aggression pacts.

questions.question: Why did the Allied powers originally support the Greek invasion of western Anatolia?

options.A: They wanted to enforce the partitioning of Turkey under the Treaty of Sèvres and secure control of the Dardanelles and Aegean coastline.
options.B: To stop communist revolution from China
options.C: To establish a joint French-Greek wine monopoly
options.D: Because the Sultan had asked for Greek assistance

questions.explanation: Britain and France backed Greek Premier Venizelos's expansionist dreams to carve up Anatolia into European zones of influence.

questions.question: In what year did Mustafa Kemal Atatürk pass away, leaving behind a modern, sovereign secular republic?

options.A: 10 November 1938 at Dolmabahçe Palace, Istanbul
options.B: 1 January 1923
options.D: 15 September 1918

questions.explanation: Atatürk died on 10 November 1938, mourned globally as one of the greatest state-builders and military geniuses of the twentieth century.

questions.question: What was the psychological impact of Atatürk's educational campaign across Anatolia?

options.A: Literacy skyrocketed as ordinary peasants learned to read and write in months rather than struggling with archaic calligraphy for years.
options.B: Schools were boycotted by parents.
options.D: People stopped using books entirely.

questions.explanation: The simplified Latin script democratized education, unlocking reading, writing, and scientific knowledge for the broad Turkish public.

questions.question: What is the synonym of the word 'resolute' in describing Mustafa Kemal's leadership?

options.A: Vacillating and timid
options.B: Steadfast, determined, and unwavering
options.D: Passive

questions.explanation: 'Resolute' means possessing firm determination, purpose, and unshakeable resolve.

questions.question: What did Mustafa Kemal do with the former Ottoman Sultan Mehmed VI (Vahideddin)?

options.A: He executed him publicly in Taksim Square.
options.B: Following the abolition of the Sultanate, the discredited Sultan fled aboard a British warship (HMS Malaya) into exile in Malta.
options.C: He appointed him Minister of War.
options.D: He gave him lifetime ownership of Ankara.

questions.explanation: Recognizing that the Turkish National Assembly held all real power, the last Sultan fled aboard a British battleship into exile.

questions.question: Identify the type of conditional sentence: 'If Mustafa Kemal had not rallied the Anatolian people, Turkey would have been carved up among European powers.'

options.A: Zero Conditional
options.B: First Conditional
options.D: Third Conditional (Hypothetical past situation with past result)

questions.explanation: 'Had + past participle' in the if-clause followed by 'would have + past participle' in the main clause defines the Third Conditional.

questions.question: What reform was introduced regarding the national calendar and clock under Atatürk's modernization?

options.A: Adoption of the international Gregorian calendar and the 24-hour metric clock
options.B: Reversion to the ancient Mayan calendar
options.D: Setting clocks backward by twelve hours

questions.explanation: Atatürk aligned Turkey's timekeeping, calendar, weights, and measures with global standards to facilitate commerce and international trade.

questions.question: What was the significance of the Battle of Sakarya (1921)?

options.A: It was the military turning point where Kemal halted the Greek advance on Ankara after 22 days of desperate combat.
options.B: It was a minor border skirmish with no historical effect.
options.C: It resulted in the surrender of Ankara.
options.D: It was a naval battle in the Mediterranean.

questions.explanation: Sakarya broke the Greek military offensive and earned Mustafa Kemal the rank of Marshal and the title 'Gazi'.

questions.question: What is the meaning of the word 'capitulations' that were abolished at Lausanne?

options.A: Military surrenders by soldiers in the trenches
options.B: Humiliating legal and financial privileges granted to foreign nationals in the Ottoman Empire, exempting them from local courts and taxes
options.D: The capital letters of the alphabet

questions.explanation: Capitulations were unequal treaties exempting European merchants from Turkish laws, which Kemal insisted on abolishing completely.

questions.question: In Wilfrid Castle's narrative, what personal characteristic made Mustafa Kemal an extraordinary commander?

options.A: His iron self-discipline, swift strategic decisiveness, and refusal to surrender even when surrounded by overwhelming odds
options.B: His reliance on astrological fortune-tellers
options.C: His habit of sleeping during battles
options.D: His surrender of tactical decisions to junior officers

questions.explanation: Kemal possessed cold tactical lucidity, supreme organizational talent, and unmatched bravery on the battlefield.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence featuring proper use of the idiom 'to turn a blind eye':

options.A: The Sultan turned a blind eye to Allied occupying troops taking over government ministries.
options.B: The doctor turned a blind eye with an ophthalmoscope.
options.C: The blind eye turned the wheel of the carriage.
options.D: He turned a blind eye to see the stars.

questions.explanation: 'To turn a blind eye' means deliberately ignoring something undesirable or unlawful.

questions.question: What was the Amasya Circular of June 1919 issued by Kemal?

options.A: A declaration that the independence of the nation is endangered, and only the nation's own determination and willpower can save it
options.B: A peace treaty with Greece
options.C: An order to burn all military armories
options.D: A tax bill for agricultural wheat

questions.explanation: The Amasya Circular was the manifesto of the Turkish revolution, asserting that national sovereignty belonged to the people.

questions.question: What is the antonym of 'sovereignty' as applied to a vassal state?

options.A: Subjugation / Servitude / Subservience
options.B: Autonomy
options.D: Dominion

questions.explanation: 'Sovereignty' means supreme, independent authority; its opposite is subjugation, servitude, or colonial dependence.

questions.question: In what way did Kemal reform primary and secondary education?

options.A: He unified all schools under the Ministry of National Education, establishing free, compulsory, co-educational scientific schooling.
options.B: He privatized all schools for wealthy elites.
options.C: He closed all rural village schools.
options.D: He banned science and mathematics.

questions.explanation: The Law of Unification of Instruction (1924) created a modern, secular, universal education system for both boys and girls.

questions.question: What was the historical impact of the Treaty of Sèvres (1920)?

options.A: It was the Allied blueprint that attempted to dismember Turkey, which Kemal and the Nationalists furiously repudiated and defeated in battle.
options.B: It granted Turkey control of Egypt.
options.C: It was signed by Atatürk in Ankara.
options.D: It brought universal democracy to Europe.

questions.explanation: The puppet Ottoman government signed Sèvres, but Kemal's National Assembly rejected it as a death warrant and destroyed it through armed victory.

questions.question: Identify the error in: 'Mustafa Kemal was more superior than any other general of his era.'

options.A: 'Superior' is a Latin comparative and takes 'to', never 'more' or 'than' ('superior to any other general').
options.B: 'General' should be pluralized.
options.D: 'Mustafa' should be capitalized.

questions.explanation: Latin comparatives (superior, inferior, senior, junior, prior) never take 'more' or 'than'; they take 'to'.

questions.question: What monumental mausoleum in Ankara stands today as the national monument to Atatürk's legacy?

options.A: Anıtkabir
options.B: Topkapi Palace
options.D: Blue Mosque

questions.explanation: Anıtkabir is the grand mausoleum in Ankara where millions of citizens and visiting world leaders pay homage to Atatürk.

questions.question: What did Kemal reply when asked why he replaced the fez with the hat?

options.A: 'A civilized, international dress is worthy and appropriate for our civilized and international nation.'
options.B: 'Because hats protect against rain better.'
options.D: 'Because the fez was too heavy.'

questions.explanation: Kemal stated that a civilized nation must reflect its progressive mindset in its outward attire, discarding symbols of medieval decadence.

questions.question: What is the meaning of the word 'anachronism' as applied to the late Ottoman court?

options.A: Something chronologically out of place, belonging to a past era and obsolete in the modern world
options.B: A clock that runs ahead of time
options.D: A famous astronomical discovery

questions.explanation: An 'anachronism' is something belonging to a former period and inappropriate for the current era.

questions.question: How did Atatürk encourage agricultural production among Anatolian peasants?

options.A: He abolished the hated 'Ashar' (tithe tax on agricultural yield), introduced modern tractors, model farms, and cooperative credit societies.
options.B: He confiscated all farmland for state palaces.
options.C: He imported all wheat from Canada.
options.D: He ordered farmers to become factory workers.

questions.explanation: Abolishing the exploitative tithe tax liberated Turkish peasants, who Atatürk hailed as 'the true masters of the nation'.

questions.question: Which of the following sentences uses the passive voice effectively to emphasize historical action?

options.A: The Republic of Turkey was proclaimed on 29 October 1923 by the Grand National Assembly.
options.B: The Grand National Assembly proclaimed the Republic of Turkey.
options.C: They were proclaiming the Republic in 1923.
options.D: Proclamation of the republic happened.

questions.explanation: The passive construction highlights the momentous historic event ('The Republic of Turkey was proclaimed') as the primary subject.

questions.question: What is the enduring historical significance of Mustafa Kemal Atatürk as presented in the FBISE textbook?

options.A: He proved that an oppressed Eastern nation could rise from the ashes of imperial defeat, repel foreign imperialism, and build an independent, progressive, modern sovereign state through sheer self-determination.
options.B: He demonstrated that foreign loans are the only way to modernize.
options.C: He showed that military dictatorships must remain permanent.
options.D: He advocated abandoning national language in favor of foreign tongues.

questions.explanation: Atatürk became an inspiration for anti-colonial movements worldwide, proving that courage, unity, and enlightenment can triumph over subjugation.
